text.tspan: ECS auto scaling: tasks (Application Auto Scaling) and instances (capacity provider + ASG)
ECS Service Auto Scaling (task level)
CloudWatch metric
(ECS service CPU)
CloudWatch alarm
Application
Auto Scaling
ECS service A
Task 1
Task 2
Task 3 (new)
Metrics: ECS service average CPU · average memory (scale on RAM) · ALB request count per target (from the ALB)
Policies: TARGET TRACKING (keep a metric at a target) · STEP SCALING (on a CloudWatch alarm) · SCHEDULED (date/time) · docs add PREDICTIVE
and SQS backlog per task. Fargate auto scaling is much easier to set up (serverless: nothing below the tasks to scale).
EC2 launch type: scale the instances under the tasks
Option 1: Auto Scaling Group scaling
• scale the ASG on CPU utilization
• adds EC2 instances over time (slower, not task-aware)
Option 2: ECS cluster capacity provider (recommended)
• automatically provisions and scales infrastructure for tasks
• paired with an ASG; adds EC2 when CPU / RAM is missing
How a capacity provider scales (docs): "managed scaling" makes ECS create a target tracking policy on the ASG using the metric
CapacityProviderReservation = instances needed / instances running × 100 (target capacity default 100%). Managed termination protection stops
the ASG terminating instances that still run tasks. Strategy: base (minimum tasks on one provider) + weight (ratio), e.g. base 2 on FARGATE,
weight 1 FARGATE : 3 FARGATE_SPOT. Fargate Spot: 2-minute warning (SIGTERM + EventBridge event), discounted, can be interrupted.
Exam
• ECS Service Auto Scaling (number of TASKS) ≠ EC2 Auto Scaling (number of INSTANCES).
• "Tasks stuck PROVISIONING / not enough CPU or memory on the cluster" → capacity provider with managed scaling (or use Fargate).
trigger
desired count +1
